title: Butterfly motif
subtitle: Four wing panels with a chain-wrapped body, 12 cm wingspan
excerpt: The butterfly motif consists of two large upper wing panels and two smaller lower wing panels, each worked as a separate dc shape and joined at a central chain-wrapped body. At 12 cm wingspan in DK cotton it is bold enough for cushion centrepieces and works equally well in 4-ply at 8 cm for finer applique.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 6 (1891), butterfly and flower applique chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet applique butterfly.
heroPrompt: A crochet butterfly applique in pale yellow DK cotton with black body and chain antennae, 12 cm wingspan, photographed flat on natural linen in soft daylight. Four wing panels, upper wings larger than lower.

crochet.gaugeText: Each finished butterfly motif measures 12 cm across the wingspan and 7 cm from antennae tip to lower wing base in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Butterfly motif
chartDefinition.caption: Upper wing: oval 10-row shape in dc. Lower wing: smaller oval in 6 rows. Body: chain bar wrapped with dc. Antennae: ch-10 loops.

glossaryTerms.definition: Working double crochet stitches around a foundation chain to cover it completely, used here to form the butterfly body.

content.text: The butterfly builds four separate wing panels — two large upper and two smaller lower — and joins them with a

body. Each wing is a small oval: dc rows that increase from the inner edge to the widest point, then decrease back to the outer tip. Working all four wings in the same colour gives a symmetrical silhouette; using a second colour for the wing centres adds an eyespot effect.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 12 g of wing colour DK cotton, 3 g of body colour. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors.

content.text: Each finished butterfly motif measures 12 cm across the wingspan and 7 cm from antennae tip to lower wing base in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.

Ch 12. Dc in 2nd ch from hook and across. (10 dc.) Turn. Row 2: Ch 1. 2dc. Dc across to last. 2dc. (12 dc.) Turn. Rows 3 to 6: Work 4 rows even. (12 dc each row.) Row 7: Ch 1. Dc2tog. Dc across to last 2. Dc2tog. (10 dc.) Rows 8 to 10: Repeat decrease row twice more. (6 dc at end of row 10.) Fasten off, leaving a 20 cm tail for assembly.

Ch 8. Dc in 2nd ch from hook and across. (6 dc.) Turn. Row 2: Ch 1. 2dc. Dc across to last. 2dc. (8 dc.) Turn. Rows 3 to 4: Work 2 rows even. Row 5: Dc2tog. Dc across. Dc2tog. (6 dc.) Row 6: Dc2tog. Dc across. Dc2tog. (4 dc.) Fasten off with 20 cm tail.
In body colour, ch 14. Dc in each ch back (working around the chain, 14dc on each side = 28dc). Sl st to join. Fasten off. This forms a stuffed-looking body bar.
Attach body colour at the top of the body. Ch 10. Sl st into the 2nd ch from hook to form a small curl at the tip. Fasten off. Repeat on the other side.

Lay the body bar vertically. Sew one upper wing to each side of the top half of the body with the wide part upward. Sew one lower wing to each side of the lower half with the wide part outward. All four wings should fan away from the body centre.

definition.title: Butterfly motif
definition.caption: Upper wing: 10-row oval from 10dc to 12dc wide and back to 6dc. Lower wing: 6-row oval from 6dc to 8dc wide and back to 4dc. Body: chain-wrap bar. Antennae: ch-10 curl loops.

content.text: Weave in all ends. Sew the assembled butterfly onto the base fabric, stitching through each wing and the body.
Handwash with the base fabric in cool water. Reshape the wings while damp.
The bee motif (crochet-animal-bee) uses a similar body-and-wing construction with a striped body. The flower motifs pair naturally with the butterfly for a garden-theme cushion panel.
